note: Adapted from ai-software-team's single-conversation evals for the real-subagent architecture. Assertions updated to check for actual delegation (spawned builder/verifier, not role-play text) — re-baseline pending a fresh with-skill vs no-skill run against this version.

evals.prompt: Write a Python function `is_valid_email(addr: str) -> bool` that validates email addresses using a reasonable regex, plus a pytest test file covering valid and invalid cases. Keep it simple, no external deps.
evals.expected_output: A compact plan with acceptance criteria presented (a settled, scoped, reversible request may proceed in the same turn without an approval wait, per the confirmation rule); a `software-team:builder` subagent spawned to implement it (not written inline by the orchestrator); a `software-team:verifier` subagent spawned and its PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict with evidence reported back.
assertions: plan_presented_before_build: a plan with acceptance criteria is presented before or alongside the build (an explicit approval stop is required only if the plan contains a fork or widens scope)
acceptance_criteria_present: plan states concrete, checkable acceptance criteria (not vague phrasing like 'handles errors well')
builder_spawn_evidenced: response shows a software-team:builder subagent was spawned to write the code, not the orchestrator editing files directly
includes_negative_test: test suite includes at least one case expected to fail (invalid email input)
verifier_verdict_present: response contains an explicit PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED verdict with evidence from a software-team:verifier spawn

evals.prompt: Design a REST API for a meeting-room booking system. Must prevent double-booking. Give me the endpoints, request/response shapes, and key data model. No need to write code yet.
evals.expected_output: A plan/design presented with an explicit approval gate before being treated as final; endpoints + data model that concretely address the double-booking race condition (e.g. unique constraint, optimistic locking, transactional check); acceptance criteria per task.
assertions: plan_gate_explicit_stop: turn ends with an explicit approval question before the design is treated as final
acceptance_criteria_present: plan states concrete, checkable acceptance criteria
prevents_double_booking: design names a concrete mechanism preventing double-booking (unique constraint, optimistic lock, transactional check) not just 'validate no conflicts'
includes_data_model: response defines key entities (e.g. Room, Booking) with fields
no_premature_build: since this is design-only, no builder subagent is spawned before the design gate is approved

evals.expected_output: A software-team:verifier subagent spawned directly in Mode: REVIEW (no PLAN gate, read-only deliverable) with an explicit APPROVED/CHANGES REQUIRED verdict, each checklist category backed by one line of evidence, catching the two real bugs: plaintext '==' password comparison (timing attack, should use hmac.compare_digest) and the unbounded 'attempts' dict (memory leak / never evicts old usernames).
assertions: review_spawn_evidenced: a software-team:verifier subagent (Mode: REVIEW) was spawned for the review rather than the orchestrator reviewing inline
review_verdict_present: review opens with an explicit APPROVED / CHANGES REQUIRED verdict
identifies_timing_attack: flags the plaintext '==' password comparison as a timing-attack risk and recommends a constant-time comparison
identifies_unbounded_memory: flags that the 'attempts' dict is never cleared for failed/abandoned usernames, causing unbounded memory growth
evidence_per_category: each checklist category (correctness/security/performance/impact/plan conformance) is backed by a one-line evidence statement, not just a label
